meta.title: The Product & Engineering Update | Dacard
meta.description: An answer-first, source-cited template for product and engineering updates to leadership, boards and staff. Worked example plus template guidance.

notice.text: Worked example. Harborline is a fictional company and every Harborline figure is illustrative. Benchmarks and frameworks are real and cited.

meta.footer: Made with [the Product & Engineering Update](https://www.dacard.ai/update) by Dacard, Darren Card's applied AI studio. Free to use and adapt with credit. Harborline and its data are fictional. Benchmarks are quoted with source and date, and survey figures are labelled as such.

slides.title: The product & engineering update built not to overclaim

blocks.text: One story for leadership, the board and the whole company. It runs from strategy through discovery, delivery and measurement to the next investments. Every number carries a source, a date and a confidence label.

items.title: Answer first
body: Each slide title is a claim you can check. The evidence sits under it.

items.title: Paired metrics
body: Every speed number sits next to the quality number it can hurt.

items.title: One source, three cuts
body: Switch the audience above. The slides change, the facts don't.

guide.label: How to use
guide.text: Read the example once as Leadership. Switch to Board to see what drops out. Turn on guidance to see the question each slide answers, the data it needs and the rule it follows.

guide.label: Pre-read
guide.text: Send it 5 business days before a board meeting. Spend the meeting on slide 18.

guide.label: Safe harbour
guide.text: Add your own forward-looking statement and confidentiality notice here.

dig_deeper: [Engineering Management, Pyramid Communication: An Actionable Guide](https://engmanage.substack.com/p/pyramid-communication) (Nov 2025). Lead with the recommendation, then the supporting arguments, then the data.

[Cedric Chin, The Amazon Weekly Business Review](https://commoncog.com/the-amazon-weekly-business-review/) (Jul 2024). A weekly metrics review works by exposing cause and effect, and depends on leadership discipline more than tooling.

[Amanda Herson, Founder Collective, Debates Over Updates](https://foundercollective.com/?p=14226) (Mar 2026). Start with what changed since the last meeting, send data ahead, and build the meeting around 1 decision.

[Product School, Product Leadership](https://productschool.com/blog/leadership/product-leadership) (Nov 2026). One story cut three ways, why this problem for teams, why this bet for executives, why now for the board.

slides.title: We win mid-market freight brokers by automating the exception, priced per load.

items.title: Diagnosis
body: Dispatchers lose most of their day to exceptions that rules engines can't handle. Incumbents sell seats, so they gain nothing when that work disappears.

items.title: Guiding policy
body: Own the exception for brokers with 50 to 500 dispatchers. Charge for loads the agent clears.

guide.question: What is our bet and what are we not doing?
guide.needs: The strategy document. If it doesn't exist, the intake interview writes this slide with you.
guide.rule: The "we will not" column is required. Test it by asking 2 engineers and a salesperson to explain the strategy in 2 sentences each.

dig_deeper: [Will Larson, Introduction for Engineering Strategy](https://lethain.com/intro-eng-strategy/) (May 2024). Diagnosis, guiding policy and coherent actions, applied to an engineering organisation.

[Lenny Rachitsky with Chandra Janakiraman, An operator's guide to product strategy](https://www.lennysnewsletter.com/p/an-operators-guide-to-product-strategy-chandra-janakiraman) (Jan 2025). A good strategy names a few focus areas and the areas explicitly out of focus.

[Roger Martin, Why the How-to-Win Strategy Choice is So Hard](https://rogerlmartin.substack.com/p/why-the-how-to-win-strategy-choice) (Nov 2025). Choose where to play and how to win together. A list of initiatives is not a strategy.
Claire Vo, The Last Roadmap (Lenny and Friends Summit, Sep 2026). Hold convictions for years and treat features as disposable.

dig_deeper: [John Cutler, Stop the (Goal) Cascade Madness](https://cutlefish.substack.com/p/tbm-305-stop-the-goal-cascade-madness) (Aug 2024). Many goal cascades are org chart cascades with no model underneath. 2 levels of goals are enough.

[Teresa Torres, When It Comes to Discovery, Something is Better Than Nothing](https://www.producttalk.org/y-oslo-2024/) (Dec 2024). An opportunity solution tree maps the path from an outcome through opportunities and solutions to tested assumptions.
[Linear, Initiative updates](https://linear.app/changelog/2025-02-13-initiative-updates) (Feb 2025). Written updates report progress and summarise work across the projects in an initiative.
[Notion on Latent Space](https://www.latent.space/p/notion) (2026). The team that owns a capability also owns the tool its agents use.

guide.question: Where did the people and the money go, and did that match the strategy?
guide.needs: A work-type label on every issue or epic, Finance actuals, model provider and tooling invoices.
guide.rule: Explain any variance over 3 points in one sentence. Show token and tooling spend next to headcount, and R&D as a share of revenue with a dated path. Agree the split with Finance before the meeting.

dig_deeper: ICONIQ Growth, The Essential R&D Board Slides (Jul 2024). Capacity across new capabilities, quality, internal productivity and keep-the-lights-on, shown for last, current and next quarters.

[Adam Ferrari, Allocating with Intent](https://adamferrari.substack.com/p/allocating-with-intent) (Mar 2025). Every R&D organisation is placing bets. Name the categories, set target percentages and track actual spend against them.

[John Cutler, Time Allocation ≠ Capacity Allocation](https://cutlefish.substack.com/p/tbm-377-time-allocation-capacity) (Sep 2025). Hours allocated are not capacity. Interruptions, rework and dependencies shape what a team can deliver.

[LinearB, engineering benchmarks 2025](https://linearb.io/blog/engineering-benchmarks-2025-devex-developer-productivity) (Jan 2025, about 3,000 organisations). Effort averages 55% new value, 20% enhancements, 15% developer experience and 10% keeping the lights on. LinearB presents these as guidance.

[SaaS Capital, Spending Benchmarks for Private B2B SaaS Companies](https://www.saas-capital.com/blog-posts/spending-benchmarks-for-private-b2b-saas-companies/) (Jun 2026, survey of more than 1,000 companies). The median spend on research and development is 22% of ARR.

guide.needs: Interview notes, prototype and experiment results, eval error analysis.

[Marty Cagan, The AI Productivity Paradox](https://www.svpg.com/the-ai-productivity-paradox/) (Jul 2026). Build to learn in discovery, build to earn in delivery. His four risks are value, usability, feasibility and viability.

[Hamel Husain and Shreya Shankar on error analysis](https://hamel.dev/notes/llm/ai-product-engineering/evals-error-analysis.html) (Jun 2026). A product manager or domain expert should read the failures.
[First Round, The Art of Evals at Figma](https://review.firstround.com/figma-ai-eval-process/) (May 2025). People at the centre of AI product evaluation.

guide.question: Is the base we build on safe, stable and getting simpler?
guide.needs: Service-level objectives and error budgets, incident data, audit status, vulnerability ageing, the debt register.
guide.rule: Tie platform work to money or risk, such as lower cloud spend, faster enterprise onboarding or avoided downtime. Report objectives and error budget in place of raw uptime. State the engineering strategy in three lines. The board gets slide 9b.

dig_deeper: [Will Larson, Steps to build an engineering strategy](https://lethain.com/components-of-eng-strategy/) (Mar 2025). Explore, diagnose, refine, set policy, then run it. Each step feeds the next.

[InfoQ, Grafana applies SLOs and error budgets to AI agent behaviour](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/10/grafana-slo-ai-agent/) (Oct 2026). Service-level objectives and error budgets can track agent quality, because a system can stay up while it becomes less trustworthy.

[InfoQ on Joy Ebertz, All Tech Debt is Not Created Equal](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/03/tech-debt-not-equal/) (QCon London, Mar 2026). Decide which debt matters with 6 questions, starting with the cost of doing nothing.
[Product School, AI-native](https://productschool.com/blog/artificial-intelligence/ai-native) (Feb 2026). Version prompts and models, log behaviour, keep an incident process for AI features.

guide.question: Are customer and business outcomes moving?
guide.needs: One North Star, 3 to 5 input metrics, each with a definition, an owner, a target and a prior period.
guide.rule: Same metrics every period. Add an external benchmark only where a sourced one exists, and write "none" where it doesn't. Split agent activity from human activity wherever agents act for customers.

dig_deeper: [Aleph and Benchmarkit, 2026 SaaS & AI Performance Benchmarks](https://www.getaleph.com/answers/net-revenue-retention-saas-2026) (Jun 2026, 342 companies, 2025 actuals). Source of the retention benchmark.

[Eric Weber, North star metrics for AI data products](https://ericdataproduct.substack.com/p/north-star-metrics-for-ai-data-products) (May 2026). An AI product's North Star measures the change in its users' downstream work. Adoption, token use and satisfaction don't qualify.
Christina Wodtke, Radical Focus (2nd ed. 2021). A light cadence for goals. Linear prefers strategy and a North Star to team-level OKRs.
ICONIQ Growth, The Essential R&D Board Slides (2024). Report adoption over several periods, never as a single point.
[Atlassian, State of Teams 2026](https://www.atlassian.com/blog/how-we-build/the-future-of-product-craft) (May 2026). 89% of executives say AI sped work up and 6% can point to company-wide return.

guide.question: Is AI making us better, or only busier?
guide.needs: Tool usage data, a pre-AI baseline, cost per engineer, the quality metrics from slide 9.
guide.rule: Report utilization, effect and cost together. Split attended tools from unattended agents. Any effect needs a baseline and a window. Adoption is never a result.

dig_deeper: [METR's 2025 trial](https://metr.org/blog/2025-07-10-early-2025-ai-experienced-os-dev-study/) (Jul 2025, 16 developers, 246 issues) found experienced developers took 19% longer with AI. In [Feb 2026](https://metr.org/blog/2026-02-24-uplift-update/) METR called that result out of date and changed its experiment design.

[Stripe, Minions](https://stripe.dev/blog/minions-stripes-one-shot-end-to-end-coding-agents) (2026). More than 1,300 merged pull requests a week with no human-written code, every one reviewed by a person.

Ramp CPO Geoff Charles (Sep 2026) put agent-written pull requests at 75% and called speed a systems problem. A Ramp data engineer described internal AI return as measured by "vibes" ([dbt Summit 2026](https://www.getdbt.com/blog/ramp-internal-ai-agents-million-sessions)).
[Vercel Ship 2026](https://vercel.com/blog/vercel-ship-2026-recap) (Oct 2026). Agents that find and fix bugs from production context.

[Shopify's AI memo](https://www.digitalcommerce360.com/2025/04/08/internal-memo-shopify-ceo-declares-ai-non-optional/) (Apr 2025). The best-known example of an explicit AI stance, which DORA lists as a capability.

guide.question: What could break the plan, and what are we doing about it?
guide.needs: A risk register with likelihood, impact, owner and date. A short list of assumptions the plan rests on.
guide.rule: 5 risks at most. Each mitigation names a person. Include model, vendor, eval and review risks alongside the usual ones.

dig_deeper: McKinsey, A new operating model for a new world (Jun 2025). 12 elements and 4 outcomes, clarity, speed, skills and commitment. It reports a 30% gap between strategy potential and delivery, even at strong companies.
[Cagan, Build vs Buy in the Age of AI](https://www.svpg.com/the-ai-productivity-paradox/) and related SVPG pieces (2025 to 2026).

[Robert Kimani, LeadDev, Your engineering strategy has a new failure mode](https://leaddev.com/leadership/your-engineering-strategy-has-a-new-failure-mode) (Oct 2026). Match how reversible a commitment is to how strong its evidence is. Platform migrations can take years to reverse.

requires.data: A risk register with likelihood, impact, owner and date

slides.title: We stopped three things this quarter to fund agent quality.

items.title: Killed, carrier marketplace
body: 3 of 12 customers said they would pay. Two engineers moved to the Agent team.

items.title: Declined, on-premise for 2 prospects
body: $310K of pipeline. It would have cost a quarter of Platform capacity and sits outside our strategy.

items.title: Paused, mobile redesign
body: No link to a current objective. Revisit in the January strategy review.

guide.question: What did we kill or decline, and what did that free?
guide.needs: A decision log. If none exists, start one this period.
guide.rule: An empty slide is a finding. Say what each stop cost and what it paid for.

dig_deeper: [Chandra Janakiraman on Lenny's Podcast](https://www.lennysnewsletter.com/p/an-operators-guide-to-product-strategy-chandra-janakiraman) (Jan 2025). Name the areas that are explicitly out of focus.
Teresa Torres (2026). Building got cheap, and that is no reason to build everything.

requires.data: A decision log

slides.title: Five bets for Q4. Three are promises, one is an experiment and one is a probe.

rows: Evals gain under 2 points by week 3
Integration losses fall from 11 to under 4 a quarter
Partner API access slips past week 2
Learn whether accounts expand. Target $0.4M expansion

blocks.text: A promise is a date we give customers. An experiment has a metric and an end. A probe buys learning and may ship nothing.

guide.question: What do we fund next and what do we expect back?
guide.needs: A one-page brief per bet with appetite, expected result, confidence and a stop rule. Each bet traces to slide 3 and to evidence on slide 6.
guide.rule: Label the commitment level. Name outcomes in the title of each bet. Five bets is the ceiling for most teams.

dig_deeper: [Lenny Rachitsky with Ryan Singer, A better way to plan, build, and ship products](https://www.lennysnewsletter.com/p/shape-up-ryan-singer) (Mar 2025) and [John Cutler on Shape Up's constraints](https://cutlefish.substack.com/p/tbm-386-understanding-enabling-constraints) (Nov 2025). Appetite, bets, fixed time with variable scope, and a circuit breaker.
Claire Vo, The Last Roadmap (Sep 2026). Features as probes, experiments or promises, with commitment stated plainly. See [ChatPRD](https://www.chatprd.ai).
ICONIQ Growth, The Essential R&D Board Slides (2024). Show the next 12 months and a longer view.

requires.data: A one-page brief per bet with appetite, expected result, confidence and a stop rule

slides.title: 60 of 64 planned roles are filled. Head of AI Quality is the hire that matters.

list: Product managers lead eval error analysis each week.
Each team owns the tools its agents use.
Weekly written project updates feed this deck. Nobody builds slides by hand.
9 engineers per product manager. 1 regretted exit this quarter.

items.title: Help needed
body: Referrals for Head of AI Quality. The profile is a leader who has run evals for a production agent and can work across product and engineering.

slides.asof: Sources: HR system, hiring tracker. As of 30 Sep 2026.

guide.question: Is the team shaped for how we now build, and where do we need help?
guide.needs: Headcount against plan by function, open senior roles, attrition, a forward 12-month view.
guide.rule: Focus on the hard hires. Name the help you want from the reader. For staff, add recognition and drop the ratios.

dig_deeper: ICONIQ Growth, The Essential R&D Board Slides (2024). Forward org chart, open leadership roles, expertise gaps.
Marty Cagan, Transformed (2024) and [A Vision for Product Teams](https://www.svpg.com/a-vision-for-product-teams/) (Feb 2025).
McKinsey, A new operating model for a new world (Jun 2025). Structure is 1 of 12 elements.
[Figma, 2026 AI report](https://www.figma.com/blog/2026-ai-report/) (Jun 2026). Developers taking part in design rose from 44% to 60% in a year.
Lenny Rachitsky with Cat Wu (Apr 2026) on how Anthropic's product team ships in days, and [The Pragmatic Engineer on Claude Code](https://newsletter.pragmaticengineer.com/p/how-claude-code-is-built).

requires.data: Headcount against plan by function, open senior roles and attrition

slides.title: We need two decisions today and one introduction.

items.title: Decide, model commitment
body: Sign a 12-month, $1.6M commitment with our primary provider for an estimated 18% saving, or stay on demand until routing ships in December.

body.p: We recommend waiting 60 days. Routing changes our volume split and this door is hard to reopen.

items.title: Decide, pricing pilot
body: Approve per-load pricing for 10 customers for 8 weeks. Revenue at risk is about $90K if all 10 pay less.

body.p: We recommend approval. Expansion is stalled under seat pricing.

items.title: Ask, introductions
body: Two or three candidates for Head of AI Quality by 15 November.

slides.asof: Decisions due at the meeting on 4 Nov 2026.

guide.question: What do you need from the people in the room?
guide.needs: For each decision, the options, the cost of each, your recommendation and the deadline.
guide.rule: Brief the CEO and chair on any miss before the meeting. If there is nothing to decide, say so and end early.

dig_deeper: [First Round Review, Board Meetings 101](https://review.firstround.com/board-meetings-101-for-early-stage-founders/) (Aug 2026). "Thoughts?" is a weak ask. Say whether you want advice, pressure-testing, introductions or a formal decision.
[Melissa Perri](https://productinstitute.kit.com/posts/the-bottleneck-isn-t-building-it-s-deciding) (2026). Deciding is now the constraint, so measure product work by decisions changed.

requires.data: For each decision, the options, the cost of each, your recommendation and the deadline

slides.title: Every number has a row in the ledger.

blocks.text: Product operations keeps the ledger and each metric owner confirms their rows before review.

guide.label: Rule
guide.text: Verified comes from the system that owns the number. Derived is computed in code. Estimated is supplied by a person. Unknown renders as a "data needed" card and is never filled with prose.

guide.label: Owner
guide.text: Product operations keeps the ledger. Each row has a named metric owner who confirms it before the review.

slides.title: One source of truth, cut three ways, on a fixed rhythm.

rows: Team-level detail, backlog, tooling. Strategy returns when it changes
Why this problem, how your work connects

items.title: Weekly
body: Written project updates in your tracker. They are the input.

items.title: Monthly
body: Regenerate the leadership cut and review it.

items.title: Quarterly
body: Board and staff cuts. Reset plan against actual. Review bets.

items.title: Yearly
body: Refresh slides 2, 3 and 4 and the plan on slide 5.

slides.title: A Claude skill will build this deck from your systems and refuse to guess.

blocks.label: Status.
blocks.text: The template is ready to use by hand today. The skill is published as version 0.4.0 at github.com/darrencard/product-engineering-update. It has been tested on synthetic companies and on one real repository's GitHub and Vercel history, not yet on a real company's full data.

items.title: Read and confirm
items.text: Answers drafted from the strategy, decision log and risk register you already keep, each with its source. You confirm them; an interview covers the rest.

items.title: Collect
items.text: Tracker, source control, hosting, analytics, warehouse, billing, CRM. CSV works too.

items.title: Compute
items.text: All arithmetic runs in code and writes to the ledger.

items.title: Draft
items.text: Titles state the computed changes in plain words. A slide with no data shows its gap beside a greyed, illustrative sample.

items.title: Check
items.text: The rules below run on every slide. One command runs every step up to the sign-off.

items.title: Review
items.text: You see a change list and sign off before the board cut renders.

items.title: Checks that will block a render

list: A figure with no ledger row
A speed metric with no quality pair
An AI productivity claim with no baseline and window
An adoption number in an outcome slot
A metric older than its reporting window
A bet with no stop rule
A figure from part of the period that does not say so

items.title: How it differs from deck tools
body: Gamma, ChatPRD, Notion agents and Linear Pulse can already turn company data into slides, documents and status summaries. This template adds the part they leave to you, which is a fixed story, a data contract per slide and rules about what you may claim.

dig_deeper: [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) and [Anthropic's authoring guidance](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices).
[Anthropic's product-management plugin](https://github.com/anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins/tree/main/product-management). Specs, roadmap and stakeholder updates.

slides.title: Every slide names the sources it needs. None requires a connector.

blocks.text: Connect what you have. A CSV or a file upload works for every system. A slide that lacks its minimum data shows a data needed block with an owner and a due date. It's never filled with prose.

Slide 1 rolls up the slides in its own cut and needs nothing new. Slide 9b condenses slides 8, 9, 10 and 13, so the board cut needs their sources too. Turn on template guidance to see what each slide needs.
